name: gwartheg y llyn
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.

attributes.attribute: The red-eared fairy cattle of Wales.
The Plant Annwn kept them below the surface of lakes.
The Plant Annwn also kept teams of white dogs called C'wn Annwn.
In Scotland and Ireland such cattle had red bodies and white ears.
The Welsh gwartheg were wholly white like ghosts.
They could breed with the stock of mortal farmers.

text: Gwartheg y llyn were the red-eared fairy cattle of Wales. The Plant Annwn, the tribe of the Otherworld, kept them below the surface of lakes beside teams of white dogs called C'wn Annwn. In Scotland and Ireland such cattle had red bodies and white ears, but the Welsh gwartheg were wholly white like ghosts. They could breed with mortal cattle and stood as a mark of the Otherworld herds.

okr.objective: Present gwartheg y llyn as the red-eared fairy cattle kept in lakes by the Plant Annwn.
